COIN is in a **confirmed, accelerating primary downtrend**, and it just produced the single most important structural event available in the data set: a **decisive break of the 2026 double-low zone (~$139)**. The stock is trading **24.6% below its 200-day SMA** and **8.7% below its 10-day EMA**, with a freshly printed **death cross (2026-11-06)** and a **14-session streak of closes below the 10 EMA**.

**Stance: Bearish / Underweight on trend. Tactically neutral. No long until price reclaims $143.69 (10 EMA) and then $157.08 (Bollinger mid).**

All indicator values below reconcile exactly with the verified snapshot — **no discrepancies found** between the `get_stock_data` CSV and `get_verified_market_snapshot`.

## 2. Structural Context: a broken 2026 range

The decline is not new; it is the third leg of a larger bear market:

**The critical structural fact:** the 2026 lows were set at intraday **$139.36 (2026-02-12)** and **$139.18 (2026-06-26)** — a zone tested twice and defended twice. The market traded through it on **2026-10-30 (low $136.89)** and has now delivered **four consecutive closes below it** (11/05: 136.82 → 11/06: 134.76 → 11/09: 136.10 → 11/10: 132.13). The 11/10 low of **$129.41 is the lowest print in the entire ~19-month dataset** provided (April 2025 → present).

That is a distribution/breakdown pattern, not a pullback inside a range. The 2026 sequence of **lower highs** (216.60 close 5/11 → 201.05 close 9/21 → 151.58 high 11/05 → 139.75 high 11/09) and **lower lows** (139.36 → 139.18 → 136.89 → 129.41) is textbook.

**Volume confirms it.** On 2026-10-30 the stock fell **−10.62%** (160.59 → 143.54) on **20.89M shares**, roughly 2.5–3× the 5.8–8.5M seen in the preceding sessions — a distribution/capitulation day. A second heavy-volume rejection occurred **2026-11-05** (12.55M shares; open 149.03, high 151.58, close 136.82 — a −9.70% close from 151.50 with an 18.08-point range). Sellers are being paid on strength.

## 3. Indicator Selection & Rationale

I selected **8 complementary indicators**, deliberately avoiding redundancy:

| # | Indicator | Why it fits this market context |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **close_10_ema** | Fastest read on the current leg; measures how stretched price is from short-term equilibrium (entry/mean-reversion reference). |

| 3 | **close_200_sma** | Strategic arbiter of bull vs. bear regime and anchor of the golden/death-cross signal. |

| 7 | **atr** | Absolute volatility for stop placement and position sizing — mandatory given ATR = 7.9% of price. |
| 8 | **vwma** | Volume-weighted trend validation: tells us whether the *average transacting dollar* is above or below price (who is trapped). |

*Supplementary context from the verified snapshot (not counted as a ninth selection): Bollinger mid 157.08 / upper 189.17 / lower 124.98, used only to frame the volatility envelope.*

I did **not** select `close_50_sma` + `boll` as trend duplicates, nor `rsi` + `stochrsi` — the redundancy rule is respected.

## 4. Indicator-by-Indicator Read

### 4.1 Moving Averages — fully bearish stack, badly compressed
| MA | Value | Price vs. MA |
|---|---:|---:|
| 10 EMA | **143.69** | price **−8.75%** (−$11.56) below |
| 50 SMA | **173.38** | price **−23.8%** below → wait, recalc: −$41.25 = **−31.2%** |
| 200 SMA | **175.18** | price **−$43.05 = −32.6%** below |

The alignment is **10 EMA < 50 SMA < 200 SMA**, and price is below all three — a perfect bearish stack.

**The 50/200 cross has whipsawed — a distinctly bearish tell:**
- **Golden cross: 2026-10-27** — 50 SMA 179.99 crossed above 200 SMA 179.67 (a margin of just $0.31).
- **Death cross: 2026-11-06** — 50 SMA 175.35 crossed back *below* 200 SMA 175.99.

That is an **8-session round trip**. Critically, the golden cross was not driven by strength: between 2026-10-16 and 2026-10-28 the 200 SMA *fell* 3.05 points (182.32 → 179.27) while the 50 SMA rose 2.68 (177.63 → 180.31). This was a **bear-market cross** — the long average collapsing into the short one — and it has now failed. Since late October the 50 SMA has rolled over (peak 180.32 on 10/28–10/29 → 173.38) and the 200 SMA has declined 16.10 points since 2026-09-11 (191.28 → 175.18). **Both averages now slope down**; there is no longer any trend argument on either horizon.

**Price is 24.6% below the 200 SMA** (on 2026-09-21 the stock was 6.4% *above* it at 201.05 vs. 188.91). This is extreme extension territory: it raises the risk of violent counter-trend squeezes, which is an argument for **smaller, tighter shorts**, not for longs.

**10 EMA detail:** COIN has closed below the 10 EMA for **14 consecutive sessions** (10/22 through 11/10). The only close above it in the last 15 sessions was 2026-10-21 (177.08 vs. 176.57). This is a persistent, one-directional short-term trend — not chop.

### 4.2 MACD — regime flipped in mid-October, still deteriorating, but decelerating
- MACD line: **−11.53** (signal −9.13; histogram **−2.40**)
- Regime change: MACD crossed below zero on **2026-10-16** (−1.03) and has fallen monotonically to −11.53 — the most negative reading in the 60-day window (from a peak of +7.37 on 2026-09-25, a **~19-point momentum swing in ~32 sessions**).
- **Nuance:** the histogram bottomed at **−3.41 on 2026-11-02** and has improved to **−2.40 on 2026-11-10**, even as the MACD line set a new low. Translation: **the downtrend is still intact, but its acceleration phase is over.** This is the classic "slow the bleeding" precursor — necessary but *not sufficient* for a reversal. It is a warning against initiating fresh shorts at the lows, not a buy signal.

### 4.3 RSI — near-oversold, with a mild positive divergence
- RSI: **32.82** — below the neutral 50, above the 30 threshold.
- It printed **29.70 on 2026-11-02** (an actual oversold tag) at a close of 137.83. On 2026-11-10 the close is **lower (132.13) but RSI is higher (32.82)** → **positive divergence**.
- Context: RSI has been in a persistent downtrend from 60.44 (2026-09-21) → 48.40 (10/21) → 41.48 (10/23) → 32.82 (11/10). In strong downtrends RSI can *stay* in the 30–40 band for weeks; the 2026-02 decline similarly saw RSI readings in the 30s while price ground lower. **Do not treat 32.8 as "oversold = buy."**

### 4.4 VWMA — the most telling volume signal
- **VWMA: 147.74.** Price is **$15.61 (−11.8%) below** the volume-weighted average price.
- VWMA has declined **every single session** since 2026-10-01 (187.53 → 147.74), a **−21.2% collapse** in the volume-weighted trend.
- **Interpretation:** the average dollar-weighted buyer of the last ~20 sessions is sitting on an **unrealized loss of nearly 12%**. That is overhead supply. Any bounce into the **$145–150** zone runs straight into the VWMA and into trapped longs wanting to exit at breakeven — which is precisely why 11/05 was rejected from 151.58 and closed at 136.82.
- Price below a falling VWMA = **sellers control the tape with conviction**, not just drift.

### 4.5 Volatility — high and expanding; hostile to large size
- **ATR: 10.39 = 7.86% of price.** A 2-ATR stop is **$20.78, or 15.7%** of the share price. This is a position-sizing emergency.
- **Bollinger:** mid **157.08**, upper **189.17**, lower **124.98**. Band width = **$64.19 = 40.9% of the mid-band** — an extremely wide, *expanding* envelope (lower band was 164.14 on 2026-10-01). Expanding bands with price riding the lower half = **trend-continuation regime, not mean-reversion regime**.
- Price (132.13) is still **$7.15 above the lower band**, so the stock is **not** yet statistically stretched to the downside on this measure — it has room to reach **$124.98** before the band becomes a hard mechanical floor.

---

## 5. Levels (all derived from tool output — reference points, not validated bounces)

**Resistance (overhead):**
1. **$136.25** — 2026-11-10 high (immediate)
2. **$139.75** — 2026-11-09 high
3. **$143.69** — 10 EMA ← *first meaningful reclaim test*
4. **$145.45 / $148.23–151.58** — 11/03 close, 10/30 open gap + 11/05 high; **unfilled gap from 2026-10-29 (close 160.59) to 2026-10-30 (open 148.23)**
5. **$147.74** — VWMA (trapped-buyer breakeven zone)
6. **$157.08** — Bollinger mid ← *trend-neutralization level*
7. **$173.38 / $175.18** — 50/200 SMA cluster

**Support (thin):**
1. **$129.41** — 2026-11-10 low, lowest print in the data set
2. **$124.98** — Bollinger lower band
3. Below $124.98: **no measured support exists in the supplied data** — a genuinely air-pocket scenario

---

## 6. Scenarios & Triggers

**Bear continuation (base case, ~55–60% weight):**
Price fails at $136.25–139.75, breaks $129.41 on expanding volume (>8M), and grinds toward $124.98. Momentum confirmation requires MACD histogram to re-widen negatively and RSI to break below 30. Target zone **$125–129**. *Trigger: daily close below $129.41.*

**Base-building / chop (secondary, ~25–30%):**
The decline stalls on fading volume (11/06–11/10 volumes of 7.6M / 6.4M / 7.4M are already below the 10/30 and 11/05 prints). Price oscillates **$130–145** while the 10 EMA flattens and RSI bases in the 35–45 zone. This is the highest-probability environment for *whipsaw losses* — both new shorts at $131 and longs at $140 are likely to be stopped out. **Best action: do nothing, or trade smaller.**

**Bull reversal (low probability, ~15%, but high-cost to miss):**
Sequence required: (1) daily close above **$143.69** (10 EMA) — breaks the 14-session streak; (2) close above **$147.74** (VWMA) — traps shorts and clears the 11/05 rejection high; (3) close above **$157.08** (Bollinger mid) — invalidates the lower-high structure. Only at step (3) does the death cross become suspect and the $173–175 SMA cluster come into play. **Partial reversal confirmation at step 2, full at step 3.**

---

## 7. Actionable Insights

1. **Do not buy the dip here.** Four consecutive closes below a twice-tested multi-month low, with price below all three MAs and below a falling VWMA, is a definition of trend continuation. The RSI/MACD-histogram divergences are *early* signals, not entries.
2. **For existing longs:** the $143.69–147.74 zone is the rational exit/reduce zone on any bounce, not a place to add. A break of $129.41 with volume should trigger hard risk reduction.
3. **For shorts (trend-following):** the higher-expectancy entry is a **rally into $143.70–147.70**, not a chase at $132. That zone is defended by the 10 EMA, the VWMA, and the trapped-buyer population. A stop above **$157.08** (Bollinger mid) is trend-invalidating and is **~1.3 ATR** from $147.70 — a defensible structure. Risk:reward toward $125 is roughly **1.7:1**.
4. **Sizing discipline is the trade.** ATR = $10.39 (7.9% of price). A standard 2-ATR stop is 15.7% of capital per share. Size at **25–50% of your normal position** so that a normal-volatility shakeout doesn't force an exit. A mechanical stop at 1×ATR ($10.39) will be hit by noise alone.
5. **Sequence matters, not levels in isolation.** Do not front-run: require a *close*, not an intraday wick. The 11/03–11/04 bounce (137.83 → 145.45 → 151.50) then 11/05 collapse (−9.70%) is a live, recent example of why.
6. **Watch volume as the tiebreaker.** A down-close on >10M shares below $129.41 is a fresh leg. Down-closes on <7M (current condition) suggest seller exhaustion and favor the chop scenario.
7. **Unverified factor, flagged:** COIN's revenues and beta are tied to crypto-asset prices and trading volumes. No crypto price data was available in my toolset, so I **cannot quantify** BTC/ETH correlation or exchange-volume trends — treat any such assertion as outside this report's evidence base.

---

## 1. Bottom Line Up Front

COIN enters this week in a **structurally improving but cyclically hostile** setup. The company-specific news flow is arguably the best it has been all year — an OCC-style **national trust charter approval** (a durable custody/institutional moat), restored **New Jersey staking access**, a **KBW price-target raise to $237 from $221**, and a legal push to preserve **single-stock perpetuals**. ---

## 2. COIN-Specific News Flow (Nov 3 – Nov 10)

### 2.1 The bull case is being rebuilt brick by brick

**National trust charter approval — the single most important item this week.** Coinbase received approval for a national trust charter, characterized by coverage as *"a major win for crypto custody."* This is strategically significant beyond the headline: a national trust charter gives COIN a federally-recognized fiduciary/custody vehicle that institutional allocators (pensions, endowments, RIA platforms) can underwrite with far less legal friction than a state-by-state money-transmitter patchwork. It also positions COIN to custody **tokenized real-world assets and tokenized fund structures** — the exact pipeline that the Securitize news implies is scaling (see below). Custody is recurring, fee-based, and rate-insensitive: precisely the revenue mix you want when transaction volumes fall.

**New Jersey staking access restored.** COIN regained staking access in New Jersey, reversing a state-level restriction. Staking is high-margin, recurring, and improves unit economics per staking-eligible asset. The read-through is that the state-by-state regulatory pressure campaign of prior years is normalizing rather than escalating.

**Single-stock perpetuals: COIN, Kalshi and Jump Trading jointly urged a judge to keep single-stock perps trading.** This is a direct bet on COIN's **derivatives/perp franchise** — the highest-take-rate product category in crypto. A favorable ruling would open a large new revenue vertical (equity perps, not just crypto perps) and extend COIN's product moat vs. offshore venues. Treat this as a **binary legal catalyst** with meaningful upside optionality.

**KBW raised its price target to $237 from $221.** A ~7% PT increase during a week when the stock fell ~4% on inflation is a notable signal: sell-side is anchoring to franchise value (custody, stablecoins, derivatives) rather than spot-volume beta. Consensus is looking *through* the current volume trough.

**Agentic economy / Brian Armstrong narrative.** Coverage highlighted Armstrong's vision for COIN in an "agentic economy" — machine-to-machine payments, where stablecoins are the natural settlement rail for AI agents. This is the long-duration optionality story: if agentic commerce scales, COIN's rails (USDC, onchain settlement, custody) capture tolls. Not a 2026 earnings driver, but it is why the stock retains a premium multiple in drawdowns.

**Anthropic IPO buzz put COIN "back on watch."** With Anthropic IPO chatter circulating, COIN is being framed as a venue for **pre-IPO/tokenized access and retail distribution of hot AI names**.
